tex_content.html:
Lemma
[strong convexity of the closed ball, modulo the lower bound and uniqueness]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-2-minimizing-interior ↗ def:dc-ch3-4-2-stronglyconvex ↗ thm:dc-ch3-3-7 ↗ prop:dc-ch3-3-6

1. ch3:4.2Assume the base-uniform lower-bound property from section 3 and local uniqueness of minimizing geodesics near $p$: there is $\beta _U>0$ such that any two constant-speed distance-realizing geodesics joining the same $q_1,q_2$ within $\beta _U$ of $p$ coincide on $[0,1]$ (the reading of the injectivity of $\exp _{q_1}$). Then there is $\beta >0$ such that the closed ball $\overline{B_\beta (p)}$ is strongly convex (section 3). This is the whole of the Proposition 4.2 for the closed ball.
Proof

\sketch

The existence, minimizing and interior clauses are section 3 (shrinkable in the radius, so the strong-convexity radius $\beta =\min (B_0,\beta _U)$ couples correctly); the closure of a closed ball is itself, so the quantifier over $\overline{S}$ reads on $\overline{B_\beta (p)}$; local uniqueness supplies the uniqueness clause. The closed ball is used because the literal open-ball statement fails at a boundary diagonal $q_1=q_2\in \partial B_\beta (p)$ (constant geodesic, interior $\{ q_1\} \not\subset $ open ball).

□
